title: Gluing fibrewise free loci through a finite admissible common refinement
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a flat morphism, and $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $(W_j)_{j\in J}$ be a finite cover of $S$ by quasi-compact open subschemes. For each $j$ suppose given a $(U\cap W_j)$-admissible blowup $b_j:T_j\to W_j$ and an open $V_j\subset X_{W_j}\times_{W_j}T_j$ surjective over $T_j$, on which the strict transform $\mathcal F_j$ of $\mathcal F|_{X_{W_j}}$ is finite locally free, meaning locally a finite direct sum of the structure sheaf. Then there is a $U$-admissible blowup $b:T\to S$, together with morphisms $c_j:T\times_SW_j\to T_j$ over $W_j$, each equipped with an admissible blowup datum relative to the inverse image of $U\cap W_j$ in $T_j$, such that the final strict transform $\mathcal F^b$ restricts on the inverse image of $V_j$ to the ordinary pullback of $\mathcal F_j|_{V_j}$. Consequently the union of those inverse images is an open $V\subset X\times_ST$ surjective over $T$, and $\mathcal F^b|_V$ is finite locally free. All admissible blowups carry their centre ideals [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], module strict transforms are those of [def-trf-module-strict-transform], and ordinary pullback and fibre products are as in [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph and finite-sequence reduction; divisors.tex Tags 080M (lemma-extend-admissible-blowups), 080N (lemma-dominate-admissible-blowups), and 080F (lemma-strict-transform-flat).

proof.text: Write $\mathcal J_j\subset\mathcal O_{W_j}$ for the specified centre of $b_j$. Its restriction to $U\cap W_j$ is the unit ideal. Glue $\mathcal J_j$ on $W_j$ to $\mathcal O_U$ on $U$ using [lemma-nagata-glue-finite-type-ideals]. The union $U\cup W_j$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-type-ideal-extension-exists] on the qcqs scheme $S$ to extend this glued ideal to a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal L_j\subset\mathcal O_S$. Thus $\mathcal L_j|_{W_j}=\mathcal J_j$ and $\mathcal L_j|_U=\mathcal O_U$. The given isomorphism in the blowup datum identifies $T_j$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_j}W_j$ throughout.

source.place: Tag 080M, lemma-extend-admissible-blowups, proof; properties.tex Tag 01PF, lemma-extend

proof.text: Set $\mathcal L=\prod_{j\in J}\mathcal L_j$ and $T=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L}S$, with structure map $b$. On any affine neighbourhood choose finite generators for each factor; their finitely many products generate $\mathcal L$, whose associated ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent. Since each factor is the unit ideal on $U$, so is $\mathcal L$, giving the required $U$-admissible datum [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. If $J$ is empty the cover condition forces $S$ empty; take the unit-ideal blowup and the empty open, and all conclusions are vacuous. Henceforth fix $j\in J$ and put $\mathcal K_j=\prod_{k\ne j}\mathcal L_k$.

Put $T_{W_j}=T\times_SW_j$ and $\mathcal A_j=\mathcal K_j|_{W_j}$. Restriction to an open induces identity maps on local rings, hence $W_j\to S$ and $X_{W_j}\to X$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The flat base-change comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map, thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] identifies $T_{W_j}$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_j\mathcal A_j}W_j$. Apply [def-nagata-blowup-product-comparison, thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal] on $W_j$. It identifies this blowup with the blowup of $T_j$ in $\mathcal A_j\mathcal O_{T_j}$, and defines $c_j:T_{W_j}\to T_j$. Extension of an ideal is generated by images of its local generators [def-nagata-extended-ideal]; this centre is finite-type quasi-coherent. On $b_j^{-1}(U\cap W_j)$, $\mathcal A_j$ and its extension are unit ideals. This open is quasi-compact, as the definition of the datum requires: $U\cap W_j$ is quasi-compact (it is the preserved open of the given datum $b_j$) and misses $V(\mathcal J_j)$, so [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] makes $b_j^{-1}(U\cap W_j)\to U\cap W_j$ an isomorphism. Thus this factorization is an admissible blowup with exactly the required preserved open.

The restriction of $\mathcal F^b$ to $X_{W_j}\times_{W_j}T_{W_j}$ is the strict transform $G_j$ of $\mathcal F|_{X_{W_j}}$ for the specified product centre $\mathcal J_j\mathcal A_j$. Indeed apply [lem-trf-module-strict-transform-flat-pullback] with $e:W_j\to S$, $j:X_{W_j}\to X$ the open restrictions, and $\mathcal I=\mathcal L$; both flatness hypotheses were checked in step 3. Its isomorphism commutes with the quotient maps from ordinary pullback. All identifications of the iterated fibre products here are the unique ones commuting with their projections [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1), restriction to opens; Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up

proof.text: Let $Z=V(\mathcal J_j)$ and $Z_1=V(\mathcal A_j\mathcal O_{T_j})$. We have $V(\mathcal J_j\mathcal A_j)=Z\cup b_j(Z_1)$. For points outside $Z$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies $b_j$ with an isomorphism; there membership in $b_j(Z_1)$ is precisely membership in $V(\mathcal A_j)$. On $Z$ both unions already contain the point. This proves the equality, with no density assumption. Let $H_j$ be the successive module strict transform, first along $b_j$, then $c_j$. Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-comparison-epimorphism] to these two centres and the product-centre isomorphism of step 3. It gives a canonical epimorphism $H_j\twoheadrightarrow G_j$ whose kernel consists of sections supported on the inverse image of $V(\mathcal J_j\mathcal A_j)$. By [lem-trf-iterated-transform-exceptional-support], $H_j$ has no nonzero sections supported there, since its stated equality of support sets identifies this subset with the total exceptional locus of the two blowups. The epimorphism is therefore an isomorphism commuting with the quotient maps. This checks the actual product centre, rather than an unspecified centre for the same composite morphism.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, module clause (1), proof; Tag 080A, lemma-blowing-up-two-ideals

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], $X_{W_j}\times_{W_j}T_j\to T_j$ is flat. On a neighbourhood in $V_j$ trivializing $\mathcal F_j$ with finite rank $r$, its stalk is $\mathcal O_{X_{W_j}\times T_j,x}^{\oplus r}$. The local ring is flat over $\mathcal O_{T_j,t}$; tensoring an injection with this finite direct sum is the direct sum of $r$ injections, hence injective. Thus $\mathcal F_j|_{V_j}$ is flat over $T_j$ by the stalk criterion [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $\widetilde V_j=V_j\times_{T_j}T_{W_j}$. Its ordinary pullback $M_j$ is flat over $T_{W_j}$ by [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback].

source.place: Tag 080F, lemma-strict-transform-flat (2); flat.tex Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, stability requirement

proof.text: The exceptional ideal of $c_j$ defines an effective Cartier divisor $D_j$ on $T_{W_j}$ by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. Apply [lem-trf-relative-flat-cartier-support] to the flat quasi-coherent module $M_j$ of step 6: it has no nonzero sections supported over $D_j$. By [def-trf-module-strict-transform], $H_j|_{\widetilde V_j}$ is precisely the quotient of $M_j$ by those sections. Restriction to an open commutes with this quotient: on every smaller open the support condition is the same condition of vanishing off the restricted exceptional locus. The quotient is therefore $M_j$ itself. Steps 4 and 5 give the asserted canonical identification $\mathcal F^b|_{\widetilde V_j}\cong M_j$.

source.place: Tag 080F, lemma-strict-transform-flat (2), absence of exceptional torsion; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1)

proof.text: Each $\widetilde V_j$ is the inverse image of the open $V_j$, hence is open in $X\times_ST$ over $b^{-1}W_j$. The latter is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. The map $\widetilde V_j\to T_{W_j}$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], applied to the given surjection $V_j\to T_j$ and $c_j$. As the opens $b^{-1}W_j$ cover $T$, their union $V=\bigcup_j\widetilde V_j$ is surjective over $T$. On a trivializing neighbourhood of $\mathcal F_j|_{V_j}$ the tensor formula for pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $\mathcal O\otimes\mathcal O^{\oplus r}\cong\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$, explicitly $a\otimes(b_i)_i\mapsto(ab_i)_i$ with inverse $(a_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i a_i\otimes e_i$. Thus $M_j$, and by step 7 $\mathcal F^b$, is finite locally free on $\widetilde V_j$. Every point of $V$ lies in one such open, proving finite local freeness on $V$.
